dmm-2011-tiebreaker-01.title: Three ways to close up four points
dmm-2011-tiebreaker-01.body:
Whatever four points are chosen, the quadrilateral $PQRS$ (joined in this order) is one of exactly $3$ closed paths through the four points (the $3$ ways to pair up the points into "opposite" pairs). Exactly one of these three paths goes around the circle in order and has no crossing sides; the other two each have a pair of crossing opposite sides. Since $P,Q,R,S$ are chosen at random, each of the three closed paths is equally likely, so the probability is $\frac13$ (independent of the $2011$).

More concretely: among the $4!=24$ orderings of the four chosen points, those that follow the circular order (in either direction, from any starting point) number $4\cdot2=8$, and $\frac8{24}=\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

dmm-2011-tiebreaker-02.title: Count the six-digit extensions (Kraft's inequality)
dmm-2011-tiebreaker-02.body:
Each phone number of length $\ell$ is the prefix of exactly $3^{6-\ell}$ strings of six digits, and because no number is a prefix of another, these sets of six-digit strings are disjoint. There are only $3^6=729$ six-digit strings in total. If $x$ numbers of length $5$ are allocated,
$$10\cdot27+20\cdot9+x\cdot3+77\cdot1\le729\ \Longrightarrow\ 3x\le202\ \Longrightarrow\ x\le67.$$

This is achievable: allocate level by level. Of the $27$ strings of length $3$ use $10$ ($17$ left), whose $51$ children of length $4$ include $20$ allocated ones ($31$ left); these have $93$ children of length $5$, of which we use $67$ ($26$ left), whose $78$ children of length $6$ leave room for the $77$ six-digit numbers. Nothing is a prefix of anything else.

**Answer: 67**

dmm-2011-tiebreaker-03.title: Generating function
dmm-2011-tiebreaker-03.body:
Let $F(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nx^n$. The sum over $i+j+k=n$ is the coefficient of $x^n$ in $F(x)^3$. The coefficients of $x^1$ and $x^2$ in $F^3$ vanish (the lowest power in $F^3$ is $x^3$), so the recursion for $n\ge3$ together with $a_1=1,a_2=0$ says
$$F=x+\tfrac12F^3.$$
All $a_n\ge0$, so for $x\ge0$ the series increases with $x$. Writing $x=F-\frac12F^3$, $x$ increases with $F$ for $0\le F<\sqrt{2/3}$, and the largest $x$ on this branch is $\sqrt{\tfrac23}\left(1-\tfrac13\right)=\tfrac23\sqrt{\tfrac23}\approx0.544>\tfrac12$. So the series converges at $x=\frac12$, and $F(\tfrac12)$ is the solution of
$$F=\tfrac12+\tfrac12F^3\iff F^3-2F+1=0\iff(F-1)(F^2+F-1)=0$$
lying in $[0,\sqrt{2/3})\approx[0,0.816)$. The roots are $1$, $\frac{-1+\sqrt5}2\approx0.618$, $\frac{-1-\sqrt5}2$, so $F(\frac12)=\frac{\sqrt5-1}2$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{2}$**
